title: Metering snapshot windows and invoice rounding rules PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Customers with mixed plans (per-token + seat + reserved throughput) have seen small but material invoice delta noise caused by inconsistent metering snapshot windows and invoice rounding rules. This PRD defines consistent snapshot window semantics for hybrid metering, rules for rounding and carry-forward credits, and acceptance criteria for billing accuracy and invoice explainability.
background: We currently compute usage on multiple subsystems: token usage per request (streaming + batch), per-seat active minutes from auth events, and reserved throughput consumption from dedicated pools. Different services use different hourly/day boundaries and rounding behavior which causes off-by-one token charges, duplicated micro-credit application, and differing invoice line totals between preview and final invoices. Finance and Support have escalated a need for deterministic, auditable snapshot semantics and a small set of explicit rounding rules to reduce disputes.
goals: Define a single canonical metering snapshot window model that all billing subsystems adhere to
Specify deterministic invoice rounding and carry-forward credit rules to avoid micro-fluctuation disputes
Ensure invoices remain explainable to customers via per-line breakdowns and stable totals between preview and final invoice
Keep customer visible changes minimal unless explicitly configurable via plan settings
non_goals: Redesign current pricing tiers or unit economics
Replace existing metering pipelines in a single release (we will iterate with compatibility layers)
Change downstream tax calculation or third-party payment reconciliation logic
user_stories: As a finance operator, I want metering windows to be consistent across subsystems so monthly invoice totals match preview totals within $0.01 for >99% of invoices
As a billing engineer, I want a canonical snapshot boundary and a deterministic rounding algorithm so debugging disputes is straightforward
As a customer, I want invoice line items to show how the final total was derived (metered units, rounding delta, credits applied)
requirements_functional: Canonical snapshot window: All usage producers must report usage into aligned hourly windows anchored at UTC hour boundaries (00:00-01:00, etc.). For monthly invoices, monthly totals are the sum of the canonical hourly windows within the billing period.

Event time vs ingestion time: If a usage event contains an explicit event_timestamp, billing must use event_timestamp to attribute the event to a canonical window; if missing, use ingestion_time but mark as estimated in debug logs.

Rounding rules: Per-line rounding should happen only at presentation; internal aggregation must use integer micro-units (e.g., micro-tokens) and store totals precisely. Final invoice rounding to currency must be performed using banker’s rounding to cents; keep per-line rounding deltas and record them in invoice metadata.

Carry-forward credits: Negative micro-balance positions smaller than $0.01 are carried forward as a pending credit into the next invoice only if the absolute value is >= $0.005 after internal micro-unit aggregation and before currency rounding.

Preview vs final invoice parity: Preview invoices generated within 24 hours of month end must use the same canonical windowing and rounding logic as final invoices. Any remaining adjustments must be explicitly labeled and justified in invoice metadata.

Backfill policy: For late-arriving events attributed to a previous canonical window, the system must write a correction record and surface a reconciliation line on the next invoice; corrections older than 90 days require manual approval process.
Explainability: Each invoice must include line-level fields: meter_id, canonical_window_range, raw_units, micro_units, pre-rounding_amount, rounding_delta, credits_applied, final_line_amount.
Opt-in plan-level tolerance: Enterprise customers may configure a tolerance threshold (in cents) to auto-absorb minor rounding deltas; default tolerance is 0 cents.

Monitoring & alerts: Generate alerts when monthly invoice deltas between preview and final exceed $5 or >0.5% for a customer, or if >0.1% of processed events were attributed using ingestion_time rather than event_timestamp in a billing period.
Backward compatibility shim: Introduce a compatibility flag for older consumers of metering RPCs so they continue receiving the pre-change envelope for 3 months after rollout.
requirements_nonfunctional: Accuracy: 99.9% of invoices must have final vs preview total parity within $0.10 after rollout in first 30 days
Performance: Canonical window aggregation must not increase billing pipeline end-to-end latency by more than 20% on average
Audibility: Full per-customer per-window trace must be retained for 12 months and queryable via the billing debug API
Resilience: Late-arrival correction mechanism must be idempotent and tolerant to duplicate events
acceptance_criteria: All usage producers return canonical_window metadata and 95%+ successfully attribute events by event_timestamp in staging
End-to-end test that injects synthetic events across window boundaries demonstrates deterministic per-hour aggregates and stable monthly totals
Finance validation: sample of 500 historical invoices reprocessed with new logic show median delta <$0.02 and 99th percentile delta < $3
Invoice explainability: generated invoice JSON contains the required per-line fields and a human-readable breakdown in the PDF/portal
Preview parity alerting configured and firing in staging when deliberately introduced discrepancy exceeds thresholds
Compatibility: legacy consumers flagged by compatibility shim continue to receive pre-change envelope for 3 months with no functional regressions
QA: no user-visible regressions in billing UI rendering for customers with mixed plan types (per-token + seats + dedicated throughput)
Operational runbook updated and circulate to Support and Finance; at least two on-call engineers trained on reconciliation flow
metrics: Preview vs final invoice delta (USD) — median, p90, p99
% events attributed using event_timestamp vs ingestion_time
# of invoice disputes logged per 10k invoices
Billing pipeline latency distribution before/after change
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Design reviews + alignment with Finance and Support (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Implement canonical window tagging and internal aggregation in staging; expose debug APIs (3 weeks)
Phase 2: Run dual-write mode where both old and new aggregates are computed for 1 billing period; run reconciliation jobs and collect metrics (1 billing period)
Phase 3: Enable default new logic for <5% of customers (canary) for 1 invoice cycle and monitor
Phase 4: Progressive rollout to all customers over next 2 invoice cycles; maintain compatibility shim for 3 months
Phase 5: Post-rollout retrospective and tuning with Finance and Support
qa_test_cases: Cross-window streaming test: stream events whose event_timestamps fall on boundaries and assert canonical attribution
Late-arrival correction test: inject an out-of-order event for previous month and assert reconciliation line appears on next invoice
Rounding edge test: construct micro-unit totals that produce rounding tie cases (exactly .005) and assert banker’s rounding applied
Preview vs final parity test: generate preview invoice 12 hours before month end and compare to final invoice after aggregation
Compatibility shim test: ensure legacy API consumer returns unchanged envelope while new consumers get canonical_window
dependencies: Billing ingestion service (ENG-54012) must add canonical_window metadata
Invoice renderer service (ENG-52390) must include per-line rounding_delta fields in PDF/JSON
Support tools team for debug UI changes (ENG-53167)
Customer success communications for enterprise opt-in tolerance
notes: We prefer UTC-aligned hourly windows to avoid daylight savings issues across regions
Banker’s rounding chosen to reduce systematic bias vs always-round-up
Carry-forward rule threshold chosen to avoid dust credits creating noise on invoices
This PRD intentionally keeps pricing unchanged; the goal is determinism and explainability
Potential follow-up: allow plan-level configuration for windowing cadence (e.g., per-minute windows) for latency-sensitive enterprise customers
